subject: SDK bootstrapping, rate-safety and endpoint cutover plan
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@integrify.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena@integrify.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick sync: SDK migration + cutover constraints

Hi Vivek,

Quick note from our side — Integrify is planning to move from Redwood SDK v1 to v2 next month. The major asks from our engineering team are: a short warmup window to populate caches, predictable rate-fencing during ramp, a safe endpoint cutover (v1 -> v2) with a fallback plan, and recommended retry/backoff patterns for our HTTP client (we run on Go).

Can you share a concise plan we can hand to our SREs? We need code-snippets for IDempotent-retries, suggested timeouts per API call, and guidance on how to stage traffic so we don't trigger rate-limits. Also — what telemetry should we validate pre/post cutover?

Target window: week of 2026-10-18.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Khan
Platform Lead, Integrify Inc.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick sync: SDK migration + cutover constraints

Samir — thanks for the clear asks. I sketched a practical runbook and a small code bundle to hand to SRE. Attaching: redwood_sdk_v2_quickstart.md and sample-backoff-snippets.py. High-level plan below; I kept it appliance-friendly for your Go stack.

1) Pre-cutover (2 weeks prior)
- Validate SDK v2 in a staging environment against a mirrored dataset. Confirm tokenization/embedding parity for a small prompt set (we'll provide a golden set).
- Warmup: run a KV-prefix preload job for your common endpoints (5–10k prefixes over 24–48h) to populate caches and prime KV caches.
- Telemetry to baseline: per-route P50/P95 latency, tokens-per-request distribution, 4xx/5xx rate, retry count, and 429 spike rate.

2) Cutover strategy (week of 2026-10-18)
- Canary (10% traffic) for first 2 hours -> monitor latency, 5xx/429, and error traces.
- Ramp to 50% over 4 hours if stable (no 5xx and 429 ≤ baseline * 1.5).
- Full shift next day (or sooner) if steady.
- Fallback: immediate rollback policy to v1 with health-check gating if 5xx > 1% or 429 sustained > baseline * 2 for 30m.

3) Retry/backoff and timeouts (Go examples in attached snippets)
- Idempotent requests: up to 3 retries with exponential backoff jittered (initial 200ms, factor 2, max 3s).
- Non-idempotent: avoid client-side retries; rely on server-side safeguards or explicit idempotency keys.
- Timeouts: default overall request timeout = 10s; streaming calls = 60s. Adjust if your median token length is high.

4) Rate-safety
- Use token-bucket client-side limiter tuned to 80% of observed sustained throughput during staging.
- Respect server-side 429 headers (Retry-After) — if seen, pause retries and back off exponentially for route.

5) Observability checklist
- Ensure tags for request.source (staging|canary|prod), route, model_version, client_id.
- Track per-client 429/5xx, retry counts, and circuit-breaker opens.

Next steps: Monica will coordinate a 45-minute technical handoff session with your SREs and provide the golden prompt set. Grace will run a quickload job template for your warmup.

I'll join the call if you want. Proposed times: Tue 2026-10-12 11:00 or Wed 2026-10-13 09:00 PT.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior CSM, Redwood Inference

Hi all — draft warmup job template attached and a quick note on sizing. For a medium-sized account like Integrify (peak QPS ~120), I recommend:
- Warmup duration: 36 hours across 3 worker pods (k8s) hitting the most common prefixes (we'll provide the list).
- Rate pacing: start at 10% of baseline QPS, increase 25% every 6 hours while monitoring 429/5xx.
- Pre-warm KV caches sequentially (by prefix frequency) to avoid hot-shard spikes.

Attachment: integration-cutover-plan.xlsx (warmup tab), also included minor sample-backoff-snippets.py adjustments for Go clients.

I'll post the exact resource estimate by EOD 2026-10-05.

— Grace

- We use a custom idempotency key for batch calls — we'll avoid client retries for those.
- For streaming conversational endpoints, should we keep client-side timeout at 120s or rely on server keepalive?

Otherwise, we'll kick off the staging deployment tomorrow and report back the initial telemetry.
